name: SongbookPro Groups
tagline: A shared song and setlist library for bands and worship teams, synced into the SongbookPro apps.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The data model here is not exotic: songs as ChordPro or PDF, setlists as ordered lists of songs, members with roles, and a sync layer. An agent can build you a self-hosted band library with transposition, autoscroll and a phone-friendly reader in a weekend, and for a five-piece covers band that is genuinely enough. What you cannot one-shot is the reason Groups exists, which is that it feeds content into SongbookPro's own native apps that your bandmates already have on their tablets. A browser PWA on a dark stage with bad wifi is a worse place to be than a native app with a real offline library and pedal support. So: buildable, but you are replacing an ecosystem with a website.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted web app where a band uploads ChordPro or PDF charts, arranges them into setlists, and each member reads them on their own device with transposition and autoscroll.
requirements: Node 20+ and a cheap VPS or a spare machine on the band's network
songs already in ChordPro text or PDF, or the patience to type them
bandmates willing to open a browser instead of their existing app
a domain or Tailscale if you want it reachable from a venue
whatYouLose: Native apps on iOS, Android, Windows and macOS that your bandmates already know and already have installed
A real offline library that does not depend on a service worker guessing right when the venue wifi dies
Page turn pedal and hardware accessory support, which browsers handle badly
Imports from other songbook formats and the accumulated file-format edge cases
Someone else owning backups of the only copy of your charts
moatNotes: The moat is not the sharing service, it is the installed base of SongbookPro apps that the sharing service pours content into.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is asking four adults to change the app they use on stage, and that is a harder sell than any subscription. Groups is cheap relative to the cost of a band arguing about file sync at soundcheck, and the people who buy it have usually already committed years of charts and annotations to SongbookPro. The service is doing the boring part, which is making one person's library become everyone's library without anyone emailing a zip file.
notes: Perfectly clonable as a website, which is exactly the problem: the value lives inside apps already on other people's tablets.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted shared songbook and setlist app for a small band. Single Next.js 15 project, App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, no external services.

Data model:
- songs: id, title, artist, key, tempo, capo, body (ChordPro text), pdfPath (nullable), tags, updatedAt
- setlists: id, name, eventDate, notes
- setlist_items: setlistId, songId, position, overrideKey (nullable), perSongNote
- members: id, name, role (leader or player), joinCode hash

Auth: one shared band join code stored hashed in .env plus a per-member display name in a signed cookie. No OAuth, no email, no accounts service. Leaders can edit, players are read-only.

Features, in scope:
- Upload or paste ChordPro text; also allow PDF upload stored on disk in ./data/files
- Write a small ChordPro parser: [C] style inline chords rendered above lyrics, {title}, {subtitle}, {comment}, {start_of_chorus} directives. Ignore unknown directives instead of crashing.
- Transposition: semitone up/down buttons plus a per-member sticky preference, sharps/flats aware
- Reader view: large type, dark mode default, one column on phones, adjustable font size, autoscroll with speed control and spacebar toggle
- Setlist builder with drag to reorder, and a setlist play mode with next/prev song and swipe
- Full text search across title, artist and lyrics using SQLite FTS5
- Export: a setlist as a single printable HTML page, and a JSON dump of the whole library

Out of scope, do not build: real time follow-the-leader sync, payments, native apps, push notifications, multi-band tenancy, telemetry.

Offline: make it an installable PWA with a service worker that precaches the app shell and caches every song and PDF a member has opened, so a phone works with no network. Show a clear banner when serving stale cached data.

Deliver: seed script with three public domain hymns, .env.example with BAND_JOIN_CODE and SESSION_SECRET, npm run dev working on a clean clone, and a README with a one-paragraph note on backing up ./data.
